conventions.general: Reference configuration is a modeling proxy for the complete host, not a published physical bill of materials. RAM capacity is reused numerically in the legacy Teads convention (no GB/GiB rescaling). Socket counts are assumptions unless explicitly stated. Guest local-disk counts are used as physical-drive proxies; no optional network storage.
conventions.azure: Largest family guest is the RAM proxy unless adjusted: Dnls uses Dns RAM; Dls/Dlds use Dsv7 RAM; Dals/Dalds use 640 GB; DCas/DCads/ECas/ECads use 768 GB; LaOSv4 uses the L96as class. F memory variants share 640 GB. Mv3 hosts use installed-memory proxies 4/16/32 TiB and 2/8/16 sockets. DCeds uses four and DCads two SSDs as explicit assumptions where only capacity is published. HBv5 uses four sockets. Other socket counts are modeling assumptions.
